figures.finding: Romania's state-aid scheme under Government Decision 421/2018, run by the Office for Film and Cultural Investments (OFIC), refunds 30% of eligible spend in Romania for projects from the 2024 call on (35% before), with a minimum Romanian budget of EUR 100,000 for a feature or per series episode and at most EUR 10 million of aid per project; the consolidated decision runs to 31 December 2026, and the culture minister announced on 4 May 2026 a three-year extension (agreements to end-2029, payments to 2031) with about EUR 55 million a year.

value.name: Schema de ajutor de stat (HG 421/2018), cash rebate
value.administeredBy: Oficiul de Film și Investiții Culturale (OFIC), Ministry of Culture

figures.applies: Romania, audiovisual works shot in Romania; terms of the decision as consolidated to 15 January 2025, extension as announced in May-June 2026.

sources.said: Prezenta schemă de ajutor de stat are caracter multianual şi se derulează până la data de 31 decembrie 2026, cu posibilitate de prelungire … ART. 4^1 (1) Începând cu sesiunea de apel de proiecte deschisă în anul 2024, ajutorul de stat acordat în baza prezentei scheme constă în decontări … în cuantum de 30% din totalul cheltuielilor eligibile realizate pe teritoriul României … a) 100.000 euro pentru … b) 100.000 euro pentru … (3) Valoarea maximă a ajutorului de stat nu poate depăşi echivalentul în lei al sumei de 10 milioane euro pentru

Producțiile beneficiază de 30% cash rebate, din cheltuielile eligibile efectuate în România și acoperă costurile totale de producție ale lucrărilor audiovizuale, exceptând cheltuieli de pre-producție și costuri promoționale / distribuție. … intensitatea ajutorului putând crește până la 60% în cazul producțiilor transfrontaliere
The continuation for another three years of Romania’s cash rebate scheme was approved on 4 May 2026, minister of Culture Demeter András announced

Romania’s cash rebate programme is to be extended by three more years until the end of 2029 for the signing of financing agreements and until 2031 for payments … will now have an annual budget of around €55m for the next three years. … Approximately 90 projects, both national and international, have applied for the rebate since its relaunch in 2024, representing an estimated local spend of over €100m, according to OFIC.

figures.finding: The National Centre of Cinematography (CNC) resumed its funding competitions in June 2026 under the amended Cinema Law, which creates a category for minority co-productions and turns production support from interest-free reimbursable loans (direct credits) into non-repayable grants.

value.form: non-repayable grants (previously direct credits, interest-free reimbursable loans)

figures.applies: Romania, from the Cinema Law's entry into operation announced in June 2026.

sources.said: “After a long period of debates and consultations, the competitions run by the National Centre of Cinematography (CNC) are being unblocked. … Under the new law, a dedicated funding category has been created specifically for minority co-productions. Furthermore, production support from the CNC will in future be in the form of non-repayable grants instead of the previous system of interest-free reimbursable loans, known as direct credits.
